note: Each question records three things separately: what the project ALREADY holds (with the file or official page), what it does NOT hold, and what single action would resolve it. An answer is only filled in when an official source states it; otherwise the answer cell is blank and flagged.

questions.question: Do we hold written permission or a licence to use official NFL data at scale?
questions.why_it_blocks: Every empirical value depends on lawfully held data. Without a licence the entire line lab is a research exercise that cannot be published as a product.
questions.we_have: The NFL Terms page itself, which forbids reproduction and systematic retrieval without prior written consent (sections 1.1 and 1.3).
questions.we_lack: Any licence, contract, email or written consent. None is in the repository and none can be created by an agent.
questions.resolution: The owner obtains or declines a licence, and records the answer here.

questions.question: Which operator, jurisdiction and market set defines a 'signal' for this project?
questions.why_it_blocks: A signal only exists relative to a named price at a named book. Without it, 'edge' has no definition and no two sessions can compute the same number.
questions.we_have: Official operator rules for spread, moneyline, total, parlay and same-game parlay, and the settlement and repricing rules that go with them.
questions.we_lack: A named primary book, the account jurisdiction, and the executable price at the moment a signal fires.
questions.resolution: Name one book and one jurisdiction; archive its prices with timestamps (S02).

questions.question: Is there any official, league-wide depth chart?
questions.why_it_blocks: The brief asks for 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacement tracking. Whether that can be an official fact or only a club opinion determines what may be published.
questions.we_have: This session opened NFL.com /depth-charts and /teams/kansas-city-chiefs/depth-chart/ (both 404), then four club pages: WAS, NYG, NE, DET.
questions.we_lack: Any official league-wide depth chart. Only club sites publish one, and NE and DET label theirs 'unofficial' in the page text.
questions.resolution: Accept club charts as the only available source, with the official/unofficial label recorded per club (S05, S07).
questions.answer: No. Club pages only, two of the four read are explicitly unofficial.

questions.question: What exactly do the injury designations mean, and what is the final word on availability?
questions.why_it_blocks: A status is only usable if its definition is fixed and its final form is known.
questions.we_have: The league's own definitions: DNP / Limited (<100% of normal reps) / Full; and Out / Doubtful / Questionable, with Probable eliminated because ~95% of Probable players played.
questions.we_lack: The inactive list as the last word: the official inactives page was empty when read on 2026-11-12.
questions.resolution: Capture inactives on game day (S04) and treat the game status report as provisional until then.
questions.answer: Definitions are official and quoted verbatim. The inactive list is the last word, and it was not available.

questions.question: How large a sample separates skill from luck at the effect sizes NFL markets allow?
questions.why_it_blocks: A leaderboard that ranks noise is worse than no leaderboard. The project already tests 18 rules on one dataset.
questions.we_have: The project's own 18-rule gate table: best raw ROI +8.41% over 607 bets, FDR-adjusted q = 0.288; 0 of 18 rules pass.
questions.we_lack: An agreed minimum detectable effect, a power target, and a pre-registered number of attempts.
questions.resolution: Publish a power/MDE calculator with the leaderboard and refuse to rank below it (S08).
questions.answer: Not answered: no power target exists. The magnitude is visible though: with 607 bets the best rule cannot distinguish +8% from zero at the stated level (q = 0.288).

questions.question: What are the reward-pool terms — sponsor, amount, jurisdiction, payout and dispute rules?
questions.why_it_blocks: A competition with rewards needs these before it can rank anything, and 'reward' has regulatory meaning in some jurisdictions.
questions.we_have: The brief's request for a leaderboard with rewards, and a fail-closed qualification standard.
questions.we_lack: Sponsor, funded amount, eligibility, jurisdiction, payout mechanics, dispute process.
questions.resolution: Write and fund the terms, or publish the leaderboard as non-monetary (S09).

questions.question: Is there an official source that says how many points a starting player's absence is worth?
questions.why_it_blocks: Without it, any 'injury-adjusted line' is invented. The brief asks for signals, and a signal needs a magnitude, not just a direction.
questions.we_have: Official injury, practice and game status for 254 players in Week 10 2026.
questions.we_lack: Any official or operator page quantifying the point value of an absence. None was found.
questions.resolution: Either estimate it from licensed price movement around official news, or state plainly that the project publishes no such number.

questions.question: Does the official injury page have a stable identity over time, so a snapshot can be trusted?
questions.why_it_blocks: A snapshot without a version cannot be cited or audited; a later reader cannot tell whether the page changed.
questions.we_have: The page title states season and week. Nothing else identifies the version.
questions.we_lack: A date, timestamp, ETag or archive on the page itself.
questions.resolution: Record the read time and the response bytes beside every snapshot (S04).

questions.question: Is the repository's own arithmetic reproducible from its committed data?
questions.why_it_blocks: If the published numbers cannot be recomputed, no downstream decision can rest on them.
questions.we_have: 24 independent recomputations in decisions/recompute.py, each from raw or committed CSV without importing project code.
questions.we_lack: Nothing for the 21 that matched. One labelling ambiguity and two blocked cells remain.
questions.resolution: Done for this snapshot; repeat on every change (S15).
questions.answer: 21 of 24 match exactly. 1 is a labelling ambiguity (MAE vs RMSE). 2 are blocked because the underlying quantity does not exist officially.

questions.question: Which of the seven parallel site builds is authoritative?
questions.why_it_blocks: A reader cannot tell which number is the project's position when seven builds disagree. Decisions get made against the wrong page.
questions.we_have: Seven live builds in one repository, each with its own verified-looking header.
questions.we_lack: A single canonical surface and a redirect or archive policy for the rest.
questions.resolution: Choose one surface and archive the others behind one labelled index (S13).

questions.question: How far do the officially published standings and the project's pinned dataset diverge today?
questions.why_it_blocks: Every model input is from a dataset frozen at 2026-10-29. Decisions made today rest on two-week-old records.
questions.we_have: The pinned dataset (last completed game 2026-10-29) and the official 2026 division standings read on 2026-11-12.
questions.we_lack: A refresh, and any statement on the page that the data is stale.
questions.resolution: Print the dataset date and auto-flag staleness (S12).
questions.answer: The dataset is 14 days stale against the official standings at the time of reading.

questions.question: Can replacement exposure (snaps) be measured from an official source?
questions.why_it_blocks: 'A backup replaced a starter' is only measurable if playing time is known.
questions.we_have: Official Next Gen Stats player metrics; the official player-stats index with 11 categories.
questions.we_lack: Any official snap-count or participation page: the direct NGS participation URL returns 404 and no snap category appears in the official index.
questions.resolution: Accept that replacement exposure is unmeasurable officially and model only declared availability (S06).
questions.answer: No official snap-count or participation source was found.

questions.question: How should a pushed or voided leg be treated in an ROI figure?
questions.why_it_blocks: Pushes change the denominator. An ROI computed without the convention is not comparable with another that uses it.
questions.we_have: The operators' own rules: a whole-number spread push is refunded; in a same-game parlay a pushed leg is repriced on the remaining legs, not refunded.
questions.we_lack: A single stated convention applied to every published performance table.
questions.resolution: State the convention on every table (S10).
questions.answer: Official settlement rules exist and are quoted; the project's tables do not all state which convention they used.

questions.question: Does a positive measured correlation actually pay, after the operator reprices the combination?
questions.why_it_blocks: The project's own conclusion depends on this. If the book reprices, a correlation that clears the naive break-even is still not an edge.
questions.we_have: The measured same-game correlations (home cover x over phi = +0.0086; home moneyline x home cover phi = +0.6724) and the operator's repricing rule.
questions.we_lack: The actual same-game-parlay price at the moment of betting, which is the only thing that settles it.
questions.resolution: Archive SGP quotes alongside single-leg quotes (S02) and compare.

questions.question: Is the practice-status signal available early enough to be actionable, or does it arrive after the price moves?
questions.why_it_blocks: A signal published after the market reprices has no value even if it is correct.
questions.we_have: The practice report as published mid-week, and the game status report as the final stage.
questions.we_lack: Any timestamped record of when each report was published versus when prices moved.
questions.resolution: Timestamp snapshots and quotes on the same clock (S02, S04).

questions.question: What does 'validate' mean for a strategy — which gates are mandatory and what are their thresholds?
questions.why_it_blocks: Without fixed thresholds, a strategy can always be declared a pass after the fact.
questions.we_have: Eight gates implemented fail-closed, and FDR control in the project's own pipeline.
questions.we_lack: Owner sign-off on the thresholds, and the number of attempts counted for multiplicity.
questions.resolution: The owner signs off the gate list and the attempt budget, and it is frozen before the next test.

questions.question: How should the project resolve a conflict between two official pages?
questions.why_it_blocks: Eight players are already unjoinable and two club charts call themselves unofficial. Without a written rule, each conflict is decided by whoever happens to be looking.
questions.we_have: Both official pages for every conflict, and the conflict list itself.
questions.we_lack: A written precedence rule and an escalation path.

questions.question: What would make the owner reject the whole leaderboard idea?
questions.why_it_blocks: A competition can be technically sound and still be a bad idea. This question is asked so the rejection criteria exist in advance rather than after a result.
questions.we_have: The stated blockers: no licence, no quotes, no power target, no reward terms.
questions.resolution: The owner answers this directly, once.
